current.text: DeMar DeRozan, Russell Westbrook and Dennis Schroder are no longer on the Kings. That leaves the ball mostly with Sabonis and Zach LaVine.
Experts expect his usage, minutes and assists to rise. They see his assists going back to about 6 and his minutes to about 33.
He is the projected starting center next to Acuff, LaVine, Hunter and Murray. Nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot. Ham calls him the Kings' best player.
Maxime Raynaud should not take his starting job or hold him to about 28 minutes.
Mike Miller runs the Kings offense this season.
Some experts pass on him because his role and the Kings' direction are unclear. It is not known yet whether the offense will run through him.
Toronto has talked to the Kings about him before. Sacramento might try to move his contract at some point.

Experts disagree on the trade risk. Most call a trade the main risk. Lloyd (October 8) thinks his contract makes a trade unlikely. They also disagree on what a trade would do: one expert says he would keep most of his value, another says he could become a 23-minute backup on a good team because he cannot defend or shoot.
The Kings are projected near the bottom of the league. Vegas has them at about 21.5 to 22.5 wins.

Experts disagree on whether the Kings will rest veterans. Lloyd expects them to trade or sit veterans. Others expect them to play Sabonis whenever he is available so they stay out of the relegation zone.
Doug Christie is under the most pressure on the Kings and may lean on veterans to win games.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an undisclosed injury.
Experts expect him to miss fewer games than last season. They also expect his FG% and 3P% to bounce back from last season's lows.
In category leagues he is about a round 3 pick (round 3 to 4 for some), with top-20 upside. He is not a first-rounder. One best/worst-case ranking puts him between 13th and 55th.
Lloyd thinks his Yahoo rank of 34 is too low.
In a mock auction, about 25 USD was called a reasonable price. He went for 24 USD.

durable.text: He is an elite, unselfish passer and the best player at assists and rebounds combined. He piles up assists and rebounds when the offense runs through him.
He needs the ball to pile up assists. Many of them come from dribble handoffs, so he creates less than his assist totals suggest.
His category profile is a high FG% on real volume, league-leading rebounds and big assists for a frontcourt player. His turnovers are high.
He has never been a steals or blocks player. He is a very poor shot blocker.
He is not a good 3-point shooter.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues. His game is hard to build around in categories when you take him early.
Last season he pulled his hamstring before the season, then had a rib injury and then knee problems. He played only about 19 games.

note: Experts put him in round 3 for categories, close to his Yahoo value of 26 USD and the 24 to 25 USD mock auction price. ESPN's average cost of 38.7 USD and our league's 41 USD last season look too high for a player whose value rests on FG% and rebounds while he gives back turnovers, threes and blocks. He fits punt TO builds best and suits teams that want FG%, rebounds and frontcourt assists. Early on, check his Yahoo Q status, whether his minutes reach about 33 and his assists about 6, and any trade news.
